advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Tighten `_WORD_TRIPLE_ALIAS` so incidental hyphenated prose triples do not falsely accept a block that still carries a rot-prone token (e.g. validate the alias against the store, or require an explicit alias context).
evidence: scripts/check_comment_hygiene.py:133-139: `_block_accepted` ORs the acceptors over the whole block text

tests/unit/test_comment_hygiene_guard.py:113-119: `test_a_word_triple_alias_accepts_the_block` deliberately accepts a block containing `run 30721408463` because a triple alias is present — confirming an incidental prose triple would do the same
This codebase's dense comments frequently contain three-word hyphenated compounds, so false-accepts are plausible in practice.
advisory.finding: The word-triple-alias acceptor regex `[a-z]{3,}-[a-z]{3,}-[a-z]{3,}` matches ordinary hyphenated prose (e.g. 'table-driven-pure', 'read-only-config'), not just store aliases. Because acceptance is evaluated per whole block, any such incidental triple anywhere in a comment/docstring falsely ACCEPTS the block even when it also contains a genuine rot-prone commit SHA or run id, silently disarming the gate for that block.
scenarios: A comment carries both a real rot-prone run-id/SHA and an unrelated hyphenated compound like 'copy-on-write' (each word >=3 chars) — the gate passes it.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile acceptor scope with CONTRIBUTING.md 'mark the line' semantics, or update the docs to state acceptance is block-scoped.
evidence: scripts/check_comment_hygiene.py:196-199: `for start, text in ...: triggers = _block_triggers(text); if not triggers or _block_accepted(text): continue` — acceptance is block-wide
CONTRIBUTING.md:156: `**Vendor-pinned external references** — mark the line with \`context: external\``
scripts/check_comment_hygiene.py:186: docstring blocks use the entire docstring text as one block
advisory.finding: Acceptors (including the `context: external` escape hatch) are evaluated per whole comment block / docstring, but CONTRIBUTING.md documents the escape hatch as 'mark the LINE with context: external'. A single acceptor token anywhere in a large module/class docstring accepts EVERY rot-prone token in that docstring, including unrelated ones on other lines.
scenarios: A long module docstring with one `context: external` for one upstream SHA also silently permits an unrelated bare CI run id elsewhere in the same docstring.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Decide whether a file that fails to tokenize/parse should be a hard error or at least reported, rather than silently under-scanned.
evidence: scripts/check_comment_hygiene.py:149-166: `try: tokens = tokenize.generate_tokens(...) ... except (tokenize.TokenError, IndentationError, SyntaxError): pass` then only appends already-collected blocks
scripts/check_comment_hygiene.py:170-174: docstring scan also returns `[]` on SyntaxError, so a syntactically-broken file is scanned for neither comments (partially) nor docstrings
advisory.finding: `_comment_blocks` swallows tokenize failures (TokenError/IndentationError/SyntaxError) via a bare `pass`, returning only comments collected before the failure. A file that fails to fully tokenize silently escapes comment scanning past the error point — an undocumented false-negative for the gate.
scenarios: A file with a syntax error after some comments: rot-prone comments appearing after the tokenize error are never examined and the gate reports clean.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a negative test: two SEPARATE (non-adjacent) comment blocks — one carrying a rot-prone token, one carrying a resolvable ticket id — assert the tree scan still returns exit 1 and reports the rot-prone block.
evidence: scripts/check_comment_hygiene.py:133 `def _block_accepted(text: str) -> bool:` searches the whole block text
scripts/check_comment_hygiene.py:155 adjacency grouping: `if line == last_line + 1 and current_lines:` — block boundaries are the untested decision surface

The suite's only multi-line/acceptor+trigger case (test_a_grouped_hex_ticket_id_accepts_the_block, lines 103-110) places acceptor and trigger in the SAME adjacent block; there is no test where a triggered block and an acceptor-bearing block are SEPARATE (separated by code/blank line) asserting the triggered block still fails
ABSENCE: no test writes two distinct comment blocks (one rot-prone, one with a ticket id) separated by a non-comment line and asserts returncode == 1
advisory.finding: The acceptor is block-scoped (`_block_accepted` searches the entire joined adjacency-block text), but no test pins that an acceptor token in one comment block does NOT leak to accept a SEPARATE, non-adjacent triggered block. The new `_comment_blocks` adjacency-grouping logic decides block boundaries, so a boundary regression (e.g. grouping non-adjacent comments, or the acceptor's scope leaking across blocks) would let a stale SHA/run-id comment slip past whenever a nearby-but-distinct comment carries a resolvable ticket id — undetected by the current suite.
scenarios: A file with a stale-SHA comment on one line and an unrelated comment citing a ticket id a few lines later — a boundary/scope regression would falsely accept the stale-SHA block
advisory.suggested_fix:
Add a test writing e.g. `# Broke in run 30721408463 here.
X = 1
# Tracked on 3006-e198-77aa-4bb2.
Y = 2
` and assert `_run(tmp_path).returncode == 1` with the run id in stdout, pinning that the acceptor does not leak across blocks.
